messages:
marta: Quick update — we flipped the compact-warmup pack for the 2x-small GPU pool a few hours ago. rolling monitor now. :eyes:
jason: Nice! Any early numbers on cold-start/warmup?
marta: p50 cold-start down ~230ms -> ~70ms on average for short prompts, p99 from ~1.1s -> ~420ms. micro-warmup reduced first-token overhead a lot.
devon: That's a solid drop. Are we seeing any change in steady-state latency or throughput with the packing enabled?
marta: Minimal impact for steady-state. Throughput +/- 1% at 95th; some microbatching alignment improved concurrency. Main win is reduced tail and fewer cold-triggered fallbacks.
kai: Can you paste the quick perf snippet you used? saves others time to reproduce.
marta: Sure — bench command we ran: ```bash
./bench_runner --model redwood-4x --pool 2x-small --seq 128 --warmup compact --runs 5000 --report p50,p95,p99
```
outputs (sample): ```
baseline: p50 320ms p95 700ms p99 1100ms
compact-warmup: p50 90ms p95 310ms p99 420ms
```
(tested across 3 hosts, avg of medians)
jason: Wow, p99 down ~60% for those cases. Any tradeoffs? more memory pressure or eviction churn?
marta: We did see a slight increase in short-lived KV entries during micro-warmup (~8% higher churn) but eviction cost remained within threshold. Memory per-worker +3-4%. No OOMs.
olivia: Anything for rollout notes — is this enabled by default for Dedicated customers or only hosted nodes?
devon: Right now it's opt-in on Dedicated; hosted will start a gradual flip next week behind the safety gate.
kai: Are there any model families this doesn't play nice with? very long seqs?
marta: For seq > 2k we saw negligible benefit because kernel warmup amortizes differently. So we gate the compact pack to models with typical seq < 512 and high short-request ratio.
perf-bot: [perf-check] Canary pass: 6/6 buckets OK, no regression on p50/p95, tail improved in 5/6.
jason: Excellent. Can we quantify cost impact?
marta: Early econ delta: ~7-12% per-token reduction for mixed short workloads because fewer fallback/edges. We'll run a 48h cost sim for more robust numbers.
olivia: Please drop a short note in release notes and product-bulletins so solutions engineering can mention this to customers.
marta: Will do. I'll file a short blurb + a graf with before/after plots in the release doc. Also adding rollout checklist: 1) enable compact-warmup flag 2) monitor perf-check buckets 3) validate KV churn 4) revert if p99 regresses.
devon: One more ask — can we expose a diagnostic metric for "warmup hits" so customers can see if they're getting the benefit?
marta: Good idea. Adding warmup_hit_ratio to telemetry for the flip.
kai: congrats team :rocket:
marta: TY! Great cross-team effort — infra, scheduler and runtime all pitched in.
